Prince William and director Karan Johar in Mumbai | Photo Credit: Special arrangement
Prince William received a Bollywood welcome at director Karan Johar’s Dharma office in Mumbai this afternoon. Currently in India for the Earthshot Prize Awards , the royal dined with actors Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan. Chef Anand Morwani curated a special menu for the occasion, featuring Indian favourites such as vada pav, Parsi keema and nargisi kofta, each with a contemporary twist.
“They approached us on Sunday, and we got the confirmation on Monday. We had two days to put together the menu and prepare,” says Anand, who is behind the Japanese restaurant Gaijin and catering company The Big Zest.
“The brief was to create a modern Indian menu. But since we are all from Mumbai, I wanted to give it a local touch. The menu captures the essence of the city, from its street food to the regional communities that make it what it is,” he says.
The menu drew inspiration from Maharashtra’s Koli fishing community and Parsi, Sindhi, Gujarati, Muslim, Punjabi and Jain culinary traditions. The chicken nargisi kofta, a close cousin of the classic British Scotch egg, was served with pineapple and poppy seed chutney. Parsi kheema got an Arabic twist, reimagined as a shakshuka with roasted bell peppers and gluten-free croutons.
Other offerings included lobster and egg akuri, mini vada pavs, dhokla and a butter garlic crab choux inspired by Mumbai restaurant Trishna. “Trishna is an iconic restaurant in Mumbai. If someone visited the city and I had to take them somewhere, that would be the place,” says Anand, a Mumbaikar with Sindhi and Maharashtrian roots.
Served as a grazing table, the spread also featured desserts such as gulab jamun cheesecake and jalebi.
Chef Anand Morwani and his partner Rohan Mangalorkar of The Big Zest
The Earthshot Prize was founded by William, Prince of Wales to promote innovative climate change solutions, and was presented in Mumbai on November 17, 2026. “India is at the forefront of climate solutions, and its innovations have immediate global application, especially when it comes to issues such as heat stress”, Earthshot Prize CEO Jason Knauf said, speaking with The Hindu . The prince was joined on this trip to India by his wife, Catherine, Princess of Wales.
